issues.description: The solution defines assembleBookstore(check: Bool) with a Bool parameter, while the problem statement and the template expect a no-argument function assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore. Additionally, Client.main() in the solution calls assembleBookstore() with no argument. This parameter mismatch will prevent the code from compiling and conflicts with the signature students are instructed to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent: remove the Bool parameter in the solution so it becomes private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } (or update the problem statement and template to require the Bool parameter and call it accordingly). Prefer removing the parameter to match the exercise instructions and the template comment.

issues.description: The conceptually single function assembleBookstore is described in the problem statement and declared (commented) in the template with the zero-argument signature `assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore`, but the solution implements it as `assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore` (introducing an unexpected parameter). This mismatch in the function signature across artifacts creates a mapping confusion: students expect and implement a no-argument assembler (per problem and template), while the solution uses a different signature, adding extraneous cognitive load and making it unclear which signature is authoritative.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore function signature consistent across all artifacts. Prefer the problem/template signature: implement `private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore` in the solution (remove the extra `check: Bool` parameter), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to require the parameter if it is intentionally needed.
